key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in the costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin, the presence of a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity and other sites, and the biopsy results confirming VTC metastasis are consistent with metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma, which is known for its ability to metastasize to distant sites, including bone and soft tissues.

rejected.label: Radioiodine-refractory Vesicular Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: The vignette does not specifically mention radioiodine refractoriness

rejected.label: Vascular Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: This is not a standard term in thyroid cancer classification

rejected.label: Paraganglioma
rejected.why: The presence of elevated serum thyroglobulin and thyroid tissue in the tumor biopsies does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: The tumor's characteristics and location do not match those typical of meningioma

rejected.label: Hereditary Angioedema
rejected.why: This condition does not typically present with a hypervascular tumor or elevated serum thyroglobulin

rejected.label: Metastatic Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the biopsy results and clinical presentation are more consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma
